facts.text: Cycling is the dominant mode of local transport and rental bikes are cheap and practical for visitors, but pedestrians who wander into the reddish-paved bike lanes are a genuine hazard/annoyance to locals — stay off them.
Coffeeshops and food stalls immediately around Dam Square and the Red Light District charge a tourist premium versus equivalent options a few canals over (Jordaan, De Pijp).
A canal-side sit-down dinner for two runs roughly €70-100; a "broodje" (sandwich) lunch or market food (Albert Cuyp Market) is €5-12 and a genuine local option, not just budget filler.
The Anne Frank House requires online advance booking, often weeks ahead in peak season — there is very limited or no walk-up availability.
Many canal-house staircases are extremely steep and narrow (a historic quirk, not a renovation gap) — worth knowing for travelers with mobility constraints or heavy luggage.
Dutch traditional food is meat/cheese-heavy (bitterballen, kroketten, cheese boards); vegetarian and vegan availability is nonetheless strong in central Amsterdam relative to much of Europe.
